method.units: EUR bn, nominal; USD converted at ECB annual average USD/EUR (2021 1.1827, 2022 1.053, 2023 1.0813, 2024 1.0824, 2025 1.13, 2026 1.1616 = Jan-Sep mean). Ranges are low/central/high, meant as ~90% intervals.
method.periods: 2022-2025 calendar years; 2026 = January-August (8 months). fossil_from_russia also gives 2021 (pre-war baseline).

switching_cost.definition: Extra cost of buying replacement fuel instead of Russian fuel: displaced volume x (replacement price - price the Russian supply would have cost), by fuel (crude, oil products, pipeline gas, LNG, coal), summed.
switching_cost.displaced_volume: D = max(0, 2021 volume x months/12 - volume bought in year), per country and fuel, from CREA tonnages (130 destinations) or Comtrade net weight (other reporters). Countries that bought more than in 2021 have D = 0.
switching_cost.replacement_share: Only the share r of D that was replaced by other suppliers is priced. Measured on EU27 Eurostat partner data as (increase of non-Russian imports)/(fall in Russian imports) vs 2021: gas 2022 1.44 (storage refill) -> capped 1.0, 2023 0.885, 2024 0.635; coal 2022 2.02 -> 1.0, 2023 0.758, 2024 0.257; oil >1 -> 1.0. 2025-2026 carry 2024 (Eurostat partner data incomplete). low r = 0.75x (gas), 0.5x (coal), 0.9 (oil); high r = 1.0 (demand reduction valued as if it cost the same premium). Applied to all countries (assumption: EU pattern representative).

premium_per_tonne.crude: low = pre-war structural differential (1 - k) x Brent, k = Russian/Brent price ratio in 2021 (0.948): quality/location premium of replacement grades; high = Brent - actual Russian realised crude price (CREA) that month = full discount forgone; central = midpoint. Brent 7.33 bbl/t.
premium_per_tonne.products: low = same structural differential as crude; high = Russian 2021 product basket price scaled with NY Harbor ULSD - actual Russian realised product price (CREA); central = midpoint.
premium_per_tonne.pipeline_gas_lng: central/high = TTF (IMF, USD/MMBtu) - Russian realised contract price (CREA, fitted to Eurostat import prices); low = Japan LNG import price (oil-indexed long-term contracts) - Russian price. 1 t pipeline gas = 1394.7 m3 (CREA density 0.717 kg/m3) x 38.1 MJ/m3 = 50.4 MMBtu (GCV assumed); 1 t LNG = 52 MMBtu.
premium_per_tonne.coal: low = (1 - k) x Newcastle (k = 2021 ratio, 0.934); high = Newcastle - Russian realised coal price (CREA); central = midpoint.
premium_per_tonne.timing: For CREA countries the premium is weighted by the monthly profile of displacement (month vs same month 2021), which captures that gas was cut in mid-2022 when TTF peaked.

switching_cost.uncertainty: low x0.9 and high x1.1 for CREA volume error; Comtrade-based countries low x0.6, high x1.5 (partner attribution, carried-forward years).
switching_cost.not_included: Capital costs of new import infrastructure (FSRUs, pipelines), government price support, and the general price spike paid on all gas/oil (only the premium on displaced Russian volumes is counted). Cross-check: Uniper alone booked EUR 13.2 bn realised replacement-gas cost in 2022.

oil_discount_gain.definition: Savings of buyers of Russian crude and oil products bought below market price, Mar 2022 onward.
oil_discount_gain.gross: Monthly: crude tonnes x (Brent x 7.33 - CREA realised price for that destination); products tonnes x (destination 2021 product price/ULSD ratio x ULSD - CREA realised price). FOB basis, before freight.
oil_discount_gain.ranges: central = gross x median published/gross ratio (0.671), low = gross x lowest ratio (0.493), high = full gross FOB discount (1.0). Published figures are net of the longer freight and compare with other suppliers delivered prices. Comtrade-based countries: global average discount per tonne, low x0.6, high x1.3.

laundered_oil.definition: Value of oil products made from Russian crude that a country imported from third-country refiners (India, Turkey, China; UAE as re-export/blending hub).
laundered_oil.model: Comtrade HS 2710 exports of each refiner country to the destination (USD) x Russian share of that refiner country crude intake (India, China: Comtrade HS 2709 tonnes from Russia/world; Turkey: CREA Russian crude / 31 Mt EPDK 2023 total; UAE: CREA Russian products / UAE product exports). 2022 x10/12. UAE 2024-25 not reported: 2023 pattern scaled.
laundered_oil.ranges: central = model x mean(CREA/model ratios, 1.0) = 0.699; low = x lowest ratio (CREA counts only named refineries); high = x1.0 (national average share applied to all exports). Where CREA published country-level windows (USA, GBR, FRA, ITA, NLD, AUS) central = mean(model, CREA anchor), low = min, high = max(model high, 1.3 x anchor).
laundered_oil.2026: Jan-Aug = 2025 x 8/12 x ULSD price ratio 2026/2025 x refiner Russian crude intake ratio (CREA, 2026 rate vs 2025). EU members x factor 0.332 (central) for the EU ban on products refined from Russian crude in third countries (from 21 Jan 2026), calibrated so the EU Jan-May total matches CREA/Novaya Gazeta EUR 0.929 bn; low x0.5 of that, high x2.
laundered_oil.caveat: Hubs (Netherlands, Singapore, UAE, Hong Kong) re-export, so country values overlap with their customers; Georgia (Batumi/Kulevi terminals) and Singapore blending are not modelled as sources.

method.fossil_from_russia: CREA payments (EUR) per destination per year; low/high +-15% (CREA certainty B). Comtrade-based: importer-reported value +-20% where observed, 0.4x-1.8x where carried forward from the last observed year; no data: 0 with high = 50% of 2021 total imports from Russia (trade.json).
method.countries_outside_crea: Comtrade importer-reported HS 2701 (coal), 2709 (crude), 2710 (products), 2711 (treated as LPG -> products premium; no pipeline link to Russia) from partner 643, 2021-2025; tonnes from net weight or value / CREA global price; 2021 from Russia-reported mirror if the importer did not report; missing later years carry the last observed year; 2026 = last x 8/12.

notes: Switching cost central EUR 133.1 bn (low 59.5, high 204.5) over 2022-Aug 2026 for all countries; oil discount gain 101.2 (72.2-154.1); laundered oil 104.2 (73.5-161.1).
Replaces build_data.py ENERGY_PREMIUM_SHARE = 0.25 of the value of Russian fuel no longer bought.
2026 includes the Hormuz-crisis oil price spike (Brent Mar-May 2026 > USD 100/bbl), which widens both the switching premium and the discount gain.
IMF monthly gas/coal prices (FRED) end July 2026; August 2026 = July value.

Laundered oil and the importer view overlap: a hub (NLD, SGP, ARE) and its customer can both carry the same barrels. Do not sum laundered oil across countries for a global total; use CREA aggregates instead.
CREA attributes pipeline gas by ENTSOG flows; transit countries (DEU, SVK, AUT, HUN, TUR) can carry gas consumed elsewhere, which shifts switching costs between neighbours.
Oil discount gain does not net out freight paid on longer voyages beyond what the published calibration estimates imply.
All values estimated; certainty: switching C (CREA countries) / D (Comtrade-based), discount C/D, laundered C (D where zero), fossil_from_russia B (CREA) / B-C (Comtrade) / D (no data).
